newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner says N.Y. harassing it over Fox.
newsitem.headline: Time Warner says N.Y. harassing it over Fox.

text.p: Time Warner Inc on Wednesday accused New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani of politically harassing the company in a dispute over the distribution of the Fox News channel in New York.

A federal judge earlier on Wednedsay issued a ruling strongly favoring Time Warner. The preliminary injunction prevents the city from forcing Time Warner to carry Fox News, a unit of Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd, on city-run cable channels.
The city government has promised to appeal the judge's ruling.
"We think this is an instance of political harassment against this company," Time Warner Corporate Counsel, Peter Haje said at a news conference.
Haje said Guiliani's support for Fox News, a 24-hour all news cable service launched last month, was highly unusual and suspect.
"While there are over 30 programmers, many based here in New York which want to get onto our systems, nobody gets this kind of treatment but Fox," Haje said.
Haje said Time Warner already carries two general news services on its New York systems, delivered to one million customers and that there was little demand for more news.
Sports, movies and educational channels were all more frequently requested by New York cable subscribers in company surveys, he said.

Haje said the preliminary injunction against New York City carrying either Fox News or news programming from Bloomberg L.P. was open-ended and would only be reversed by an Appeals court or after a trial.
Haje said Time Warner was open to a negotiated settlement of its dispute with News Corp but that no talks were underway.

News Corp, a leading international publisher and entertainment group, has many commercial relations with the Time Warner media conglomerate, which were unlikely to be disturbed by the dispute, Haje said.
In a separate written statement, Time Warner Chairman Gerald Levin hailed the court ruling as a victory for U.S. constitutional rights.
"The principal at stake went far beyond Time Warner's cable operations in New York City. Every one interested in the integrity of the First Amendment should be gratified," Levin said.

The commercial importance to News Corp of securing New York City carriage for the Fox News channel goes beyond nearly adding a substantial number of new viewers because the city is the home of the U.S. advertising industry.
